name: Face slimming mask (Japanese lifting mask)

card.summary: An elastic strap or mask worn over the chin, cheeks and ears to hold the lower face upward, used for a tighter-looking jawline and less visible puffiness while worn.
card.aka: Lift-up mask, V-line mask, V-line lifting mask
card.note: Fit matters: reviewers on retail sites mention tight ear loops and skin irritation; no clinical trials of these straps were found.

quick.overview:
A face slimming or lifting mask is a stretchy, reusable band, sometimes with a sheet or gel panel, that wraps under the chin and over the ears or head. Wearers use it for a short session or overnight with the aim of a firmer-looking jaw and a sharper V-shaped lower face.

The look change described by users is a tighter feel and sharper line while it is worn. No clinical trials of these products were found, and patents describe the concept as a face-lifting mask held by elastic bands.
quick.how: Users put the strap on clean skin, adjust it so the chin is supported and the band runs over the ears or crown, and wear it for a set period or while sleeping. Some designs add a moisturizing or anti-wrinkle sheet or acupressure points over the nose, as described in patent filings. It is often combined with facial massage and skincare.
quick.risks: Common complaints in consumer listings are bands that are too tight over the ears and breakouts under the strap. Anyone with skin conditions or sensitivities may find prolonged occlusive contact irritating.

lead: The Japanese-style face slimming mask, also sold as a lift-up or V-line mask, is a stretch band or shaped mask that supports the chin and cheeks and is fastened over the ears or head. It belongs to a family of beauty devices that promise a firmer lower face, tapered jawline and reduced appearance of a double chin through gentle upward pressure while worn.

Patent filings describe the basic design: a standard-head-size face-lifting mask impregnated with moisturizing and anti-wrinkle substances, fixed by elastic bands over the nose with acupressure points provided [1], and a cosmetic face-lifting mask with thermal insulation [2]. These documents describe construction, not outcomes.

No published clinical study has tested a consumer lifting strap for jawline change, and no peer-reviewed assessment of these products was found. Claims about results come from sellers and from user reviews on retail sites.

angle.text: The band holds the lower face in an upward position and compresses soft tissue, so users see a sharper jawline and less visible puffiness while wearing it and shortly after. It is used as a short-term cosmetic aid, often with massage.

paras: Designs range from a simple chin-and-ear strap to sheet-style masks. Patent literature describes a face-lifting mask of standard head size, soaked with moisturizing and anti-wrinkle substances and fixed with elastic bands over the nose, with acupressure points included [1]. Another filing describes a cosmetic face-lifting mask with thermal insulation [2].
Consumer listings describe reusable silicone or elastic bands sold as chin straps for sleeping and V-line shaping. This article does not cite specific brands.

The mechanism proposed by sellers is mechanical: upward tension supports the chin and jowl area and holds the skin taut, giving a tighter appearance while worn. Where a moisturizing sheet is included, hydration may plump skin temporarily [1].

No studies found. Unrelated surgical literature uses the term mask lift for a facelift technique in which tissue of the upper two-thirds of the face is dissected and suspended, as described in a 1991 British Journal of Plastic Surgery paper; it is a surgery, not a wearable device [3].

Consumer reviews on retail listings describe both a tighter, more sculpted feel after wearing and complaints about tight ear loops and breakouts under the strap. These are individual accounts, not controlled data.

timeline.event: A patent filing describes a cosmetic face-lifting mask with thermal insulation [2].
A patent publication describes a moisturizing face-lifting mask fixed by elastic bands [1].
